messages.text: For a Wireless Communication use case involving Wi-Fi 7/8, where would Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow?

Short answer: In a Wi‑Fi 7/8 wireless communication workflow, the **Signaling Tester** fits in the **R&D / design-verification stage**, while the **Non-signaling Tester** fits mainly in the **production RF test stage**.[5][1]
| Workflow stage | Tester type | Placement and role |
|---|---|---|
| R&D / development / design verification | **Signaling tester** such as **R&S CMX500** | Used while developing WLAN devices, because RF TX/RX characteristics must be measured under **real-world conditions in signaling mode**; it lets R&D engineers test device operation across latest cellular and non-cellular standards in a single-instrument setup.[5] For Wi‑Fi 7, it supports test needs around **MLO**, multiple RF chains, **2x2 MIMO**, 6 GHz out-of-band discovery, coexistence, and E2E capabilities.[5] For Wi‑Fi 8, the CMX500 is positioned as a one-box signaling tester with Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn RF signaling test context, including prototype next-generation WLAN device testing before final IEEE ratification.[17][20] |
| Production RF test / manufacturing | **Non-signaling tester** such as **R&S CMP180** | Used in the WLAN device production phase, where **all RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time**; the CMP180 is positioned as optimized for this production RF testing purpose.[1] Its role is RF generation/analysis for production wireless device testing, with support for technologies including **Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz**, and bandwidths up to **500 MHz**.[1][2] It can also validate a **480 MHz WLAN waveform** in loopback mode, described as a potential candidate waveform for yet-to-be-defined Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn, not a formal Wi‑Fi 8 specification.[1] |
【推論】A practical Wi‑Fi 7/8 workflow would place the signaling tester first for connected, real-world R&D validation, then use the non-signaling tester later for fast RF measurements in production.[5][1]  
Limit: the cited R&S Wi‑Fi 7/8 material is PR / demonstration positioning, not a formal datasheet, configuration guide, certification document, complete test-case list, or proof of full Wi‑Fi 8 conformance coverage.[8][19]
